decision: PI APPROVAL OF BASS LOCATOR REPAIR: the Stage 2 pre-target locator is replaced so it is reliably audible on every item, with the 15 labels already recorded under the previous locator PRESERVED unchanged.
provenance: Explicit PI instruction in the current session: selection of locator specification and disposition of the offset-0 window marker.

defect.description: The 1 kHz, 20 ms, -18 dBFS pre-target locator was not audibly masked by frequency. Its in-band margin over the local FullMix was +12.5 dB. The defect was LEVEL: the cue sat BELOW the local music's loudness on 11 of 60 items, worst on item 50 at -5.4 dB.
defect.binding_constraint: CLIPPING, NOT AUDIBILITY. The natural windows already peak at -0.60 dBFS, so no cue can hold a combined peak below that. The operative limit is the natural peak inside the cue span.

approved_locator_rationale.frequency_hz_4000: Worst-case local FullMix component at 4 kHz is -48.5 dBFS, the lowest of every frequency evaluated (1 kHz -31.3, 2 kHz -36.6, 3 kHz -43.9, 5 kHz -46.3, 6 kHz -45.9), so the cue sits furthest above the local spectrum.
approved_locator_rationale.peak_level_dbfs_minus_7: -6 dBFS is the loudest level that does not clip when summed with the natural window; -3 dBFS and above were measured clipping. -7 dBFS keeps 0.52 dB of guard.
approved_locator_rationale.single_20ms_pulse: Keeps the cue inside a short span, which both preserves headroom and makes it unambiguous which blip marks the target.
approved_locator_rationale.offset_0_window_marker: REMOVED by explicit PI decision. With a louder locator the offset-0 tone was an unnecessary second tone of a different level, and the window start is already unambiguous.

audibility_evidence.metric_inband: cue peak level minus the local FullMix component at the cue frequency, in the cue's own 20 ms span
audibility_evidence.metric_broadband: cue peak level minus the local FullMix RMS in the cue's span
audibility_evidence.not_numerically_validated_only: The PI made the perceptual choice by ear; the numbers bound the choice and are recorded, but do not replace the listening judgement.
